Subject: Post-call: Tool calling integration patterns & next steps

Thanks again for a great discussion today — really appreciate the level of detail from your engineering team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

Recap:
- Goal: Integrate tool/function calling into FinApps' document ingestion + Q&A flow; surface authoritative sources and allow safe outbound actions (e.g., update customer record).
- Primary workflows: 1) Data retrieval (search + DB lookup) -> 2) Rerank with embeddings -> 3) Structured tool call for actions (create/update) or follow-up suggestions.
- Constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data classification for some customers, need for audit logs and deterministic retries for actions.

Key integration items we covered:
- SDK setup & auth: recommend short-lived OAuth tokens for private deployments; API keys for hosted if wrapped in your internal proxy.
- Routing & model variants: route low-latency UI queries to smaller quantized models; route complex reasoning to full-precision variants with fallback policies.
- Structured output / tool calling: define explicit tool schemas (name, input schema, idempotency key, permissions) and prefer strict JSON schemas for parsing.
- Embeddings & rerankers: use semantic search + dense vector reranking; consider a lightweight lexical filter pre-pass to reduce false positives.
- Parallel tools & error handling: run non-conflicting read ops in parallel; serialize mutations and use optimistic concurrency + idempotency keys for retries.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Share architecture diagram and mutual action plan (attached).
2) Neha to provide a short sample tool definition + example structured output spec by Mon 03/01.
3) Schedule a 45-minute follow-up with your engineering + security reps to map auth and audit requirements — propose Tue 03/03 10am PT.

- Alex: confirm attendees for Tue 03/03 and provide any required compliance docs ahead of time.

If this looks good I’ll lock in the follow-up.

Hi Alex — quick technical notes and a sample tool definition you can review ahead of Tue’s call. High-level answers first:
- RBAC & key rotation: Hosted API supports scoped API keys with environment tags + rotate-by-creation timestamp; Dedicated/Private supports integration with your KMS for short-lived certs and OIDC for service accounts. Audit logs for tool calls are stored with request_id and user_id metadata.
- Tool-level permissions: define a permissions matrix per tool (callable_by: [roles], allowed_models: [ids], allowed_scopes: [read,write]). Redwood evaluates permissions at the routing layer before executing.
- Embeddings latency: for a 1k-doc corpus, a two-stage approach (sparse filter -> vector similarity -> single-model rerank) typically sits around 120–220ms on our bench with a tuned index; under 300ms is feasible depending on network and infra.

Sample tool definition (JSON-ish, abbreviated):

"""
{
  "tool_name": "update_customer_record",
  "description": "Idempotent mutation to update customer billing metadata",
  "input_schema": {
    "customer_id": "string",
    "fields": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true},
    "idempotency_key": "string"
  },
  "permissions": {
    "callable_by": ["support_agent","automations"],
    "allowed_models": ["redwood-qa-1","redwood-llm-2"],
    "audit_level": "high"
  },
  "retry_policy": {"max_retries": 3, "backoff": "exponential"}
}
"""

Integration pattern notes:
- Parallelization: run pure reads (search, embedding lookups, knowledge-base calls) in parallel; only serialize when hitting mutation tools. This reduces tail latency.
- Error handling: use an idempotency_key for mutations so retries are safe; for transient read errors, retry with jitter; for permanent errors return structured error objects with error_code and suggested_fallback_action.
- Structured output: ask model to return a single top-level JSON object that matches the tool input_schema. Validate server-side before execution.
- Security: sign tool calls with short-lived tokens and log the original request_id and model response hash for non-repudiation.

I’ll join Tue and bring a short slide with sample call flows. I’ve attached a short sample JSON schema to the Drive folder (link in the HubSpot deal).

—Neha
